text: When Rehoboam's rule was firmly established and he had grown strong, he abandoned the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD.
He came with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, and troops beyond counting who came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites.
He captured the fortified cities of Judah and advanced as far as Jerusalem.

Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the officials of Judah who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, "This is what the LORD says: You have abandoned me, so I in turn have abandoned you to the hand of Shishak."
Then the officials of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."

When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them. I will grant them a measure of deliverance, and my wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.

versions.text: When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them. I will grant them deliverance before long, and my wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כִּמְעַט לִפְלֵיטָה most naturally means a partial or limited deliverance rather than a deliverance that comes soon. The following verse ('Yet they will become his servants') confirms that the rescue is incomplete, not merely imminent. 'A measure of deliverance' preserves that nuance and reads smoothly aloud.

text: Yet they will become his servants, so that they may learn the difference between serving me and serving the kingdoms of other lands."

So Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem and carried off the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields that Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and entrusted them to the officers of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the royal palace.
Whenever the king went to the house of the LORD, the guards would carry the shields, and afterward they would return them to the guardroom.
Because he humbled himself, the LORD's anger turned away from him, and he was not destroyed completely. Indeed, there was still some good in Judah.

King Rehoboam established himself firmly in Jerusalem and continued to reign. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel in which to put his name. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
He did what was evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.

The events of Rehoboam's reign, from beginning to end, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, along with the genealogies? There was continual warfare between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, and his son Abijah succeeded him as king.
